facts.text: Emmet was founded as a railroad town in 1873 by Emmet Elgin, an Irish employee of the Cairo & Fulton Railroad.
Emmet sits near the headwaters of the Terre Rouge Creek watershed, which flows northeast for 17 miles before joining the Little Missouri River.
The town’s early economy included a factory that built horse‑drawn carriages and horse saddles, reflecting its 19th‑century transportation needs.
Emmet’s first depot agent and later first postmaster was Robert Francis Elgin, who also helped survey neighboring towns.
Emmet is part of the Ark‑La‑Tex tri‑state region, linking Arkansas, Louisiana, and Texas culturally and economically.
